Shuttle Tracker shows you the real-time locations of the RPI campus shuttles, powered by crowd-sourced location data.\n\nThe map is automatically refreshed every 5 seconds. Green buses have high-quality location data, and red buses have low-quality location data. In colorblind mode, the green buses are replaced by buses with an aqua target/scope icon, and the red buses are replaced by a purple dial icon. When boarding a bus, tap \"Board Bus\", and when getting off, tap \"Leave Bus\". You must be within 20 meters of a stop by default to board a bus.

Privacy Policy
Effective Date: 10-03-2025

Shubble (“the App”) respects your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we handle your information.

Information We Collect
The App may access your device location in order to:

Show you the closest shuttle stop.
Calculate how far you are from that stop.

We do not collect, store, or transmit your location data or any other personal information. All processing happens locally on your device.

Use of Information
Location data is used only in real time to display shuttle stop information.

Your location data is never stored, logged, or sent to our servers.

Sharing of Information
We do not share your location or any other personal information with third parties.

Children’s Privacy
Shubble does not knowingly collect, store, or share personal information from children.

Changes to This Policy
If we make changes to this Privacy Policy, we will update it here and revise the “Effective Date” above.

Contact Us
If you have any questions or concerns about this Privacy Policy, you can contact us at:
Joel McCandless
mail@joelmccandless.com

If you opt in to analytics, then Shuttle Tracker will send anonymous usage data to our server. These data include your app settings, feature usage frequency, and other similar metrics. No analytics data are ever collected unless you explicitly opt in. You can see a record of recently uploaded analytics reports or opt-in status in Settings > Analytics.

Shubble is developed by the Rensselaer Center for Open Source by your fellow RPI students. As an open source application, anyone can help develop the RPI Shuttle Tracker regardless of experience! Any contributions are welcome, as well as feedback for our current team.
